title: Three options or four
statement: Should a choice question default to three options, as research favours, or include the extra option a course review asked for?
detail: The assessment packet records the tension: a review asks for at least four options, while the multiple-choice evidence summary says research generally favours three and keeps four as the default only when a third plausible, diagnostically useful wrong option exists (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/assessment-item-agent.md`). The packet bars filling a fourth slot with an implausible option and leaves the default to a human decision (the same file; `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/README.md`). A meta-analysis of 80 years of research found three options optimal (Rodriguez 2005, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1745-3992.2005.00006.x). To settle it: decide the default, then count how often students choose each fourth option. Either way, no slot is filled with an implausible option, since a weak option only adds cues (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`, line 2006).
against: A packager gate that demanded exactly four options was found to over-restrict a delivery format whose real floor is 2-6+ (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0241-alpha-read-contract-investigation-and-packager-build-2026-06.qmd`). The course-quality standard declines to fix a number: "No fixed option count belongs in the universal standard" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, line 770).

evidence.quote: The MCQ BrainLift says the research consensus generally favors three options and recommends four as Alpha's default only when a third plausible, diagnostically useful distractor exists. Do not fill a fourth slot with an implausible option.
decide the three-versus-four-option MCQ policy when a fourth plausible distractor cannot be written;
arpack's "exactly 4 choices" gate over-restricts vs the API's real 2-6+ floor

The discipline: if you cannot write a third plausible distractor for a given item, use three options rather than adding filler. A weak fourth distractor is worse than no fourth distractor because it provides testwiseness cues and wastes time.
Most items cannot sustain more than two plausible distractors; the third and fourth distractors in 4- and 5-option items are typically non-functioning (selected by fewer than 5% of examinees).
First, four options reduce the guess rate from 33% to 25%

while the MCQ BrainLift reports a research consensus favoring three and recommends four as Alpha's default only when all distractors remain plausible and diagnostically useful. An agent must not resolve this by adding filler
**MCQs need ≥4 options.** A 2-option yes/no is a 50/50 guess.
Claim boundary: No fixed option count belongs in the universal standard.
mcq must have exactly 4 options

three options, exactly one defensible.

deliveries must be a list of three
Four options. Not two, not three.

- **Default option count:** 4 - **Three-option exception:** Use three options only when an independent cold review finds that a fourth misconception- or error-grounded distractor cannot be written without filler, cueing, or ambiguity; record reviewer, reason, and candidate fourth option rejected.
Four options are the default and three require a recorded no-filler exception after independent cold review.
No fixed option count belongs in the universal standard.
